cost: THE SUBJECT LANDS ON THE FLOOR OF HIS BAND AND THE CEILING IS HIS OWN BIG VECTOR. 53 against 55 +-3. Ken Norman '94's big verdict is 48.7862 x 1.1305 = 55.15, so even at d_bigness 1.00 he prints 55 and not a point more — the number his ruling names is EXACTLY his big vector, which is why the round is a class question and not a weight question. At the foot this round takes (45) his share is 0.80 and he reads 53. Measured over the whole family: foot 52 -> 49, 50 -> 51, 48 -> 52, 46 -> 53, 45 -> 53, 42 -> 54, 40 -> 54, 35 -> 54. Every foot from 54 down to 35 holds all 135 anchors, so the anchors are NOT what stops the round at 45 — the worst move on the board is. At 42 and below a second card (Dominique Wilkins '97) reaches +8, and he DECLINED recal_132 for two cards rising 10+. 45 is the last foot at which nothing on the board moves by 8.

45 IS NOT A NEW NUMBER AND THAT IS THE ROUND'S WHOLE DEFENCE OF IT. DEF_RP_LO = 45 is recal_93's own rim-protection foot for the MIDDLE clause, chosen there for the same bar and the same question. Clause 1's own 55 becomes the point of saturation, exactly as recal_118 made r64's 68 a saturation point rather than a threshold. Two constants in, zero constants added.

THE TWO CARDS THAT FALL ARE THE CLAUSE'S OWN SEMANTICS, NOT COLLATERAL. Dominique Wilkins '86 and '87 go 60 -> 58, and they are the only down-movers on the board. Clause 1 is a CLASS statement — it says which of the two d_score verdicts grades this man — so when it engages on a card whose PERIMETER vector reads above his big one (Wilkins '87: perimdisrupt 56, drb 41), the card falls. That is what the standing clause already does to him at rimprot 55; the ramp only means he meets it earlier and gently. recal_99's lift-only guard was NOT reused here because it belongs to a clause that is a claim about deterrence; this one is a claim about class, and a class statement that only ever lifts is not a class statement.

COLLATERAL IS 32 CARDS ON DEF, 30 UP and 2 DOWN, mean +2.06, max +7 and max -2. NOTHING ON THE BOARD MOVES BY 8 OR MORE ON ANY SCALE. Only three cards move by 5 or more (Dominique Wilkins '97 +7, Ken Norman '94 +7, Mike Mitchell '83 +5) and seven by 3 or 4. OVR follows on 20 cards, max +3 (the subject) and max -1. OFF moves on ZERO cards, every attribute moves on ZERO, and the top 50 by OVR has no entrant, no leaver and no rank flip. The movers are ONE archetype and read like it: scoring forwards with real size, no perimeter sheet and no jumper — Dominique Wilkins '86-'97, Mike Mitchell '81-'84, Glenn Robinson '97-'02, Alex English '85/'91, Orlando Woolridge '91/'92, Lamond Murray, Greg Kelser.

WHAT THE ROUND DOES NOT FIX, and a later ruling would have to name it. Clause 1's other two tests are still HARD. `3pt < 45` is the sharper of them: Ken Norman '95 is rimprot 46 with 3pt 53 and reads 45, so one bar the clause is not about still switches his class outright — the same defect recal_99 found on the deterrence clause and answered with a ramp there. It is left because his ruling is about '94 and because a fade on that test moves a much larger population (every shooting forward with size) than the ruling justifies. `rimprot >= perdef` is left on purpose: it is recal_99's own guard and it is what keeps this a class statement.

THE BAND ANCHORS ARE NOT TOUCHED AND recal_90's WARNING DOES NOT APPLY. Every one of the 32 movers is below the 93 knee, where band() is the identity, so DEF_TOP (104.25) and OFF_TOP (102.75) are byte-identical and not one card above the knee moves. The top 12 by DEF is identical name for name.

notes: THE DEFECT IN ONE SENTENCE: after recal_93 ramped d_bigness's middle clause and recal_99 the deterrence clause, CLAUSE 1 was the last hard 1.0 left in the function — and it decides which of two d_score formulas grades a card, a gap of 15 to 23 printed points, on the word `>=`.

IT IS THE SAME DEFECT THOSE TWO ROUNDS NAMED, ON THE CLAUSE THEY BOTH DECLINED TO OPEN. recal_93: 'the first two clauses are UNTOUCHED and still return a hard 1.0: clause 1 already reads defensive shape (rimprot >= perdef)'. Reading defensive shape is why the clause is RIGHT; it is not why the clause may STEP. recal_99 then found the identical step one clause down and wrote the identical fix.

THE STEP IS VISIBLE IN THE POOL AND NOT ONLY ON THE SUBJECT. Of the cards this clause actually decides — shape-path, 3pt < 45, rimprot >= perdef — the 27 at rimprot 52-54 average d_bigness 0.17 and DEF 52.4, and the 12 at 55-57 average 1.00 and DEF 57.8. Five rating points of one bar, five and a half printed points, and nothing in between.

THE SUBJECT DECOMPOSED. Ken Norman '93 -> '94 is a quiet decline: rimprot 61 -> 53, perdef 43 -> 38, drb 61 -> 62, perimdisrupt 14 -> 11, 3pt 16 -> 36. Nothing on his sheet moves by fifteen and DEF moves by fifteen (61 -> 46), because at rimprot 61 clause 1 gave him the WHOLE big verdict and at 53 he fell through to the middle clause's product, which reads 0.0914 for him. His big vector is 48.79 x 1.1305 = 55.2 and his perimeter vector 45.2 — the ruling's number is his big vector, to a tenth.

MEASURED BEFORE APPLYING, on the whole pool at ten settings of the foot — 54, 52, 50, 48, 46, 45, 42, 40, 38, 35 — the subject reads 46, 49, 51, 52, 53, 53, 54, 54, 54, 54 and the mover count runs 0, 12, 18, 25, 31, 32, 46, 48, 48, 52. All 135 anchors hold at every one of them; the binding constraint is the worst move on the board, which crosses +8 at a foot of 42.

OFF MOVES ON ZERO CARDS BY CONSTRUCTION, and it is verified rather than asserted. is_big() is untouched, so p['big'], recal_55's big hub, recal_91's stretch-big floor, the OVR cap branch and the marginal percentile classes all read exactly what they read before — the same separation recal_93 and recal_103 established when they moved d_bigness and left the boolean alone.
